evidence.basis: Recovered-value average; $4.10 per short ton divided by the quotation's $20.67 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: The recovered value of the ore milled from 1901 to 1904 ranged from $3.60 to $5.70 per ton (gold at $20.67 an ounce); the average was $4.10 per ton.

evidence.basis: Average of 613 development samples; $5.97 per short ton divided by the quotation's $20.67 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: During the development of the mine 613 samples were taken that were said to average $5.97 in gold per ton (gold at $20.67 an ounce).

evidence.basis: Reported average content of 143.5 tons produced
evidence.verbatim_quote: According to an engineer's report, made by F. C. Lincoln in 1936, the mine produced 143½ tons of ore with an average content of 0.965 ounce of gold per ton in 1914.

evidence.basis: Lower endpoint of the reported shipment-average range for 75 tons
evidence.verbatim_quote: According to Lincoln's report, 75 tons of ore averaging 1.25 to 3.83 ounces of gold per ton is said to have been shipped from this property from 1892 to 1894.

evidence.basis: Reported dump/shaft sample average; $7 per short ton divided by the quotation's $35 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: The Ragged Top Mines has sampled numerous dumps left from trenching and from sinking several shallow shafts along veins. The ore is said to average about $7 in gold per ton (gold at $35 an ounce).

evidence.basis: Average mill-feed grade for the last three months of operation
evidence.verbatim_quote: According to an engineer's report by C. R. Wilfley in 1928 the average grade of ore milled during the last 3 months of operation in 1925 was 0.426 ounce of gold and 4.63 ounces of silver per ton, or about $11.50 a ton at metal prices current in 1925.

evidence.basis: Reported ore average; $8 per short ton divided by the quotation's $20.67 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: The ore is said to have averaged about $8 in gold per ton (gold at $20.67 an ounce).
evidence.years: historic operations through 1913; assay year not stated

evidence.basis: Engineer-estimated available-ore grade; $10.20 per short ton divided by the quotation's $35 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: From old records of production, mill tests, and sampling by early operators, one engineer has estimated that about 980,000 tons of ore is available with a grade of $10.20 in gold per ton (gold at $35 an ounce).

evidence.basis: Carload test assay; $4.80 per short ton divided by the quotation's $20.67 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: A carload of ore taken from the first and second levels was shipped to Denver for testing. The ore assayed $4.80 in gold per ton (gold at $20.67 an ounce).

evidence.basis: Lower endpoint of the reported sulfide-body range; $7 per short ton divided by the quotation's $35 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: A 300-foot drift on the 200-foot level has disclosed a sulfide ore body said to run $7 to $10 a ton in gold (gold at $35 an ounce).

evidence.basis: Lower endpoint of the recent-sample range; $3.50 per short ton divided by the quotation's $35 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: Recent sampling is said to have shown the ore to range from $3.50 to $7 in gold per ton (gold at $35 an ounce).

evidence.basis: Reported outcrop-sample average; $10.15 per short ton divided by the quotation's $35 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: Assays of samples taken along the outcrop north of the shaft are said to average $10.15 in gold per ton (gold at $35 an ounce); south of the shaft the outcrop is barren.

evidence.basis: Average of 177 assays; $83.03 per short ton divided by the quotation's $20.67 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: According to an early publication, 177 assays made during 1902 and early in 1903 averaged $83.03 in gold per ton (gold at $20.67 an ounce).

evidence.basis: Prospect-shaft sample; $11 per short ton divided by the quotation's $35 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: Samples from the 70-foot prospect shaft, near the top where the vein was 9 inches wide, assayed $11 in gold per ton (gold at $35 an ounce).
evidence.years: sample reported by present owner before 1940

evidence.basis: Ore-bin sample; $3.50 per short ton divided by the quotation's $35 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: A sample taken from a small quantity of ore left in the bin assayed $3.50 in gold per ton (gold at $35 an ounce).

evidence.basis: First South Dakota School of Mines head assay; $10.40 per short ton divided by the quotation's $35 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: Two metallurgical tests were run on samples of the ore at the South Dakota School of Mines. The head assay for the first lot was said to be $10.40 in gold per ton and a second lot containing 150 pounds ran $14 in gold per ton (gold at $35 an ounce).
evidence.years: test date not stated; reported by 1940

evidence.basis: Grab sample from approximately 3 tons of dump quartz; $1.05 per short ton divided by the quotation's $35 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: A grab sample taken from about 3 tons of quartz on the dump assayed $1.05 in gold per ton (gold at $35 an ounce).

evidence.basis: Reported developed-quartz average; $8.50 per short ton divided by the quotation's $20.67 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: A considerable tonnage of quartz averaging $8.50 in gold per ton (gold at $20.67 an ounce) is said to have been developed.

evidence.basis: Quartz-pile sample representing last shaft ore; $7 per short ton divided by the quotation's $35 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: A second sample from a pile of quartz, apparently representing the last ore that was mined from the 65-foot shaft, assayed $7.00 in gold per ton (gold at $35 an ounce).

evidence.basis: Lower endpoint of group averages from 176 samples; $2.70 per short ton divided by the quotation's $20.67 per troy ounce
evidence.verbatim_quote: According to an unsigned report 176 samples were cut from various exposures on the vein. Average assays of various groups of samples ranged from $2.70 to $3.90 in gold per ton, supposedly based upon gold at $20.67 an ounce.
